IBNKATHIR-FULL (الجمهور): The majority interprets the summons as one to give testimony already borne; a witness must answer when personally required, otherwise the duty is communal. {"id": "2:282/q54", "question": "What does تسأموا mean?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "2:282/q54/p1", "position": "Saʾama means growing weary or irritated.", "reasons": "MUQATIL (author): Do not tire of recording even a small amount through its due date: writing better records the term and protects property, is just, reliable for testimony, and less likely to create doubt. AKHFASH (author): تسأم is from the verb سئمت, with the listed verbal nouns سآمة, سأمة, سآما, and سأما. IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB (author): ولا تسأموا means do not grow tired. TAB-FULL (author): Do not grow weary of recording a small or large debt until its term; a written record keeps track of both the due date and amount. TAB-FULL (author): The verb تسأموا means “do not tire”; Labīd and Zuhayr use سئمت in the sense of becoming weary. ZAJJAJ (author): The author argues that the next command not to tire of writing reinforces that giving testimony from the outset is obligatory. ZAJJAJ (الراجز): A rajaz poet uses السآمة for weariness, illustrating the verb سئمت. NAHHAS (author): The anonymous verse سئمت تكاليف الحياة is cited as usage evidence for the verb سئمت. THALABI (author): Tasʾamu means grow weary; the cited lines by Zuhayr and Labid attest the verb for tiring of life or its length. THALABI (author): An may be a verbal noun object, meaning tire of writing it, or governed by an omitted preposition, meaning tire of writing it. WAHIDI-BASIT (الحسن وأبو إسحاق): Al-Ḥasan says the duty covers both undertaking and delivering testimony when the person is available and has no excuse; Abū Isḥāq chooses this view, supported by the adjacent command not to tire of documenting what one witnessed. WAHIDI-BASIT (author): Saʾāma means weariness or annoyance; the infinitive clause is accusative as the object of that weariness, and the pronouns in write it and its due date refer to the debt. WAHIDI-BASIT (author): The command not to tire of writing is best addressed to creditors: document the rights they lend, small or large, with due date and term; the passage begins by addressing asset and debt holders, while trivial amounts are not normally recorded. JISHUMI (العامة): The common reading uses second-person feminine/masculine address in لا تسأموا. JISHUMI (author): Saʾam means weariness or boredom, becoming annoyed with something. JISHUMI (author): An alternative construction supplies the omitted preposition من: do not tire of writing it. JISHUMI (author): Do not tire of documenting the debt, whether small or large, and continue through its due date; another view refers to the witness’s term. KASHSHAF-FULL (author): A reading has yāʾ for both occurrences of ‘they grow weary.’ KASHSHAF-FULL (النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم): A Prophetic saying says a believer does not say ‘I am lazy’; weariness can mean laziness, a hypocrite’s trait. KASHSHAF-FULL (author): Frequent debtors may tire of preparing a separate document for each small or large debt. TABRISI (author): Ḍalāl originally means loss or going where something cannot be found; saʾam is weariness, and أقسط means acted justly while قسط means acted unjustly. | mentions 54:47 TABRISI (author): The command may address witnesses and mean not to tire of recording testimony; the stronger referent of its term is the debt's due date, not the witness's allowable period. IBNJAWZI-ZAD (author): Do not grow weary of re

cording small or large debts customarily deferred, through their due date; the document is more just, strengthens testimony by reminding witnesses, and more nearly removes doubt. RAZI-FULL (author): Saʾāma means weariness or irritation; the instruction encourages writing small and large debts because even a small dispute can grow into serious conflict. QURTUBI-FULL (الأخفش): Al-Akhfash explains the verb for becoming weary as boredom and gives its verbal nouns; an unnamed poet illustrates weariness after eighty years of life. BAYDAWI-FULL (author): Do not tire of recording any debt, small or large and brief or detailed, until its agreed due date; that refers to writing. NASAFI-FULL (الشاعر): A poet uses s-simt to express becoming weary with life after eighty years, supporting the sense of ولا تسأموا as do not tire. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): Saʾm and saʾāma mean boredom or irritation with something. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): “Become weary” is explained as “be lazy” or “be annoyed”; grammarians debate whether saʾima takes its object directly or through a preposition. A hadith and 4:142 are parallels for laziness. | mentions 4:142 ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): The pronoun in “write it” refers to the earlier debt or nearby right, equivalent in sense; those with many debts might tire of documentation. SAMIN-DURR (author): Saʾam and saʾāma mean weariness, boredom, and annoyance with something. SAMIN-DURR (السلمي): Al-Sulami reads the clause with third-person yāʾ, matching his reading of ‘they tire of writing.’ IBNKATHIR-FULL (author): Dihya and Usāma b. Zayd were affiliated with Kalb b. Wabara of Quḍāʿa; Quḍāʿa was variously said to descend from ʿAdnān, from Qaḥṭān, or to be an independent branch, and Ibn Kathīr leaves the matter to God. IBNKATHIR-FULL (author): Do not grow weary of recording a debt, large or small, through its due date; writing deferred claims is more just before God, strengthens testimony by helping witnesses remember, and reduces doubt in disputes. BIQAI-FULL (author): People must not tire of documenting either small or large debts through their due date; the separate warning magnifies a duty people might neglect. BURSEVI (author): Do not tire of documenting a debt, large or small, whether summarized or detailed, through its agreed due date. ALUSI-FULL (author): Some take saʾama as laziness by euphemism, since the Qurʾan describes hypocrites as praying lazily; a hadith says a believer should say prayer feels burdensome, not lazy. | mentions 4:142 ALUSI-FULL (author): Saʾama means to tire of or become annoyed by something; the verse discourages weariness over recording debt. IBNASHUR-FULL (author): The small and large debts represent trivial and substantial amounts; since small transactions are more frequent, parties are told not to tire of recording them. IBNASHUR-FULL (author): The prohibition concerns the result of weariness—leaving the debt unwritten—because involuntary boredom itself cannot be prohibited. IBNASHUR-FULL (author): Another interpretation takes sāmah as a figurative expression for laziness and laxity. TABATABAI (author): He defines the key terms: mutual debt, dictation, shortchanging, weariness, causing harm, disobedience, and the two plural forms for pledged collateral. BINTSHATI-IJAZ (الراغب): Al-Raghib sharpens the sense to weariness from repetition or prolonged duration, citing Qur'anic usage and Zuhayr's poem about life's burdens. | mentions 41:38, 41:49 BINTSHATI-IJAZ (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas's gloss of sa'ama as lassitude describes a result or outward sign of weariness, rather than a separate basic meaning."}]}
{"id": "2:282/q55", "question": "What does the pronoun in أن تكتبوه refer to?", "turns_on": "The notes offer different readings, referents, grounds, or applications.", "positions": [{"id": "2:282/q55/p1", "position": "The pronoun denotes the debt or right", "reasons": "TAB-FULL (مجاهد): Mujāhid says the object to be written is the debt. WAHIDI-BASIT (author): Saʾāma means weariness or annoyance; the infinitive clause is accusative as the object of that weariness, and the pronouns in write it and its due date refer to the debt. JISHUMI (author): The pronoun in تكتبوه refers to the debt/right owed. JISHUMI (author): The pronoun in إلى أجله may refer to the debt's term or to the witness's term of eligibility; the debt's term is the stronger reading. KASHSHAF-FULL (author): Mentioning debt supplies the antecedent for ‘write it,’ improves the wording, and distinguishes deferred from immediate debt. KASHSHAF-FULL (author): ‘Write it’ can refer to the debt or right; small or large describes the debt, or the document’s concise or full length without omission. IBNATIYYA-FULL (الطبري): Al-Tabari takes the pronoun in “his guardian” to refer to the right/debt and cites reports from al-Rabiʿ and Ibn Abbas. IBNATIYYA-FULL (author): La tasʾamu means ‘do not tire’; ṣaghīran and kabīran are circumstantial descriptions of the object, with the small item mentioned first for emphasis. Repeated debt recording could make people weary of writing. IBNJAWZI-ZAD (الضحاك): Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd say the pronoun refers to the debtor, so his guardian dictates. RAZI-FULL (author): The pronoun in أن تكتبوه must refer back to either the debt or the right mentioned earlier. NASAFI-FULL (author): The pronoun in أن تكتبوه may refer to the debt or the document; small or large can describe the debt's value, supporting salam in textiles, or describe a concise or detailed record. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): The word dَayn supplies the pronoun in fa-ktubūhu; it also disambiguates tadāyantum, emphasizes the reference, and generalizes to any size or type of debt. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): The pronoun in “his guardian” refers to the debtor, one of the three vulnerable cases; al-Zamakhsharī identifies an executor, agent, or interpreter who dictates with the debtor's approval. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (الطبري): Al-Ṭabarī takes the pronoun to refer to the debt, making the guardian the creditor; this is also related from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Rabīʿ. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): The pronoun in “write it” refers to the earlier debt or nearby right, equivalent in sense; those with many debts might tire of documentation. SAMIN-DURR (author): The pronoun in ‘write it’ may refer to the debt or the right; the latter is nearer, though it also means the debt. SAMIN-DURR (author): منه attaches to يبخس, with من marking origin and the pronoun referring to the debt; alternatively it is an omitted adjective of an indefinite, fronted as a circumstantial. SAMIN-DURR (author): The pronoun in وليه refers to the debtor when he has one of the three stated limitations; بالعدل repeats the earlier construction. SAMIN-DURR (author): The pronoun in فاكتبوه returns to دين; that noun is repeated to provide an antecedent, disambiguate reciprocal تداينوا, or indicate every amount of debt. BURHAN (الزمخشري): Al-Zamakhshari says debt is stated explicitly so the pronoun in write it has an antecedent. BURHAN (author): The usual order puts the pronoun's antecedent first, as in the debt verse; in another construction the first object is delayed so the pronoun refers to the nearer second object. ALUSI-FULL (قيل): Some say dayn is mentioned to provide an explicit antecedent for the later pronoun; others say it improves the wording, but the objection that tadāyantum already supplies the sense is answered because it does not clearly identify the debt itself. {"id": "2:282/q60", "question": "How does writing steady testimony?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "2:282/q60/p1", "position": "Writing makes testimony firmer by preserving exact details.", "reasons": "IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB (author): أن تضل means that one woman forgets the testimony and the other reminds her; Moses' phrase uses ضالّ for forgetful. | mentions 26:20 IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB (author): أقسط means more just; the record strengthens testimony because it reminds witnesses of all they witnessed.
